highlights: Taking over the Top Supporters board is now a real moment on screen. It always announced out loud, but nothing was ever drawn for it — so the one crown your non-buying viewers can win was invisible. It gets its own celebration card and confetti now, in your theme’s colours.

The jumbotron reacts while the Hype Meter is running. The meter itself already got faster and brighter as the room heated up, but the big screen sat still. It now breathes and pulses in step with the room, escalating through four levels — so chat can see their spamming working without looking at the small meter.
All of it follows whichever theme you have picked, and eases off automatically on the Lite effects setting.

Label printing on direct-USB label printers is fixed for real. The fix in 1.0.29 did not work — it swapped one error for another — so if printing has been failing for you, this is the update that sorts it.

Ryli sits slightly louder in OBS by default, and this update nudges her level on setups that already exist rather than only new ones. It only moves the volume slider — your mute, monitoring and visibility settings are left exactly as you set them. Move her wherever you like afterwards and RYLI will not touch it again.

Switching something on from the Ryli panel inside your Whatnot window now updates the matching control in Settings straight away. It was always taking effect; the Settings page just kept showing the old state until you clicked away and back.
Reworded the announcement about someone being just outside the top 3 — it sounded too much like a live bid.

Label printing works again on direct-USB label printers. If Windows display scaling is set above 100% — which it is on most laptops — every print failed with an error about column counts. Nothing needed changing on your printer; it just prints now.

The jumbotron no longer gets stuck on "waiting for bid". If a lot ended without a new one starting straight after, the centre screen could stop rotating through your boards and cards for the rest of the show.

Groundwork for tracking down two harder problems: the wake word missing you, and the jumbotron freezing. Nothing is sent anywhere — this only writes to a local file, and only when you launch RYLI in diagnostics mode.

Ryli now has her own volume slider in OBS. RYLI adds a source called RYLI Audio with its own fader in the Audio Mixer, so turning your Desktop Audio down to control a browser or your music no longer turns Ryli down with it. It sets itself up — you should just see it appear.
If your viewers could never hear Ryli, this is likely why. Without her own channel her sound only reached your stream through Desktop Audio, so a setup without that capture sent nothing at all.
Balance her voice against the sound effects on the Dashboard, under Audio mixer. Use the OBS slider to turn all of Ryli up or down against your mic.
New Test both button in Settings → Connections. Ryli speaks, then a bid sound plays, so you can watch the meter move and set your levels against something real.
Reset levels in OBS puts everything back if a source gets deleted, muted or hidden. Apart from that, RYLI never touches a volume slider you have set yourself.
Labels no longer go missing on fast back-to-back auctions, and a print that may already be coming out is never repeated.
The Dashboard sidebar is reordered, and a few panels and pop-ups no longer clip their own text.

RYLI now works on a Mac, running inside Parallels. Keep OBS on the macOS side and press Connect & Add Overlay to OBS exactly as normal — RYLI finds it on its own. There's a Mac section in the setup guide at ryli.app/setup-guide.html.

Two-computer setups are supported. If OBS runs on a second PC, switch on "Let OBS on another computer load my overlay" in Settings → Connections → Advanced, then restart RYLI once. Windows will ask you to allow RYLI through the firewall — choose Allow.
If OBS turns down your password, RYLI now tells you so and where to find the right one, instead of just saying it couldn't connect.
Security and privacy improvements. Nothing changes in how you use RYLI — your overlay, themes and layout are untouched.
Backups no longer store your API keys or OBS password. Restoring on the same computer keeps them as they are; setting RYLI up on a new computer, you'll enter them once.

The sponsor listing is now called Donate. Put a listing named Donate in your Whatnot shop — add whatever you like after the word — and every buyer gets a spoken shout-out and a place on your sponsor board.
Action needed if you use this: rename your $ponsor listing to Donate. The old name no longer counts.
Settings → Sponsors is now Settings → Donation Detection, with the setup steps on the page.
Whatnot joins Follow-Me. Add your handle and it rotates through the jumbotron with your other socials.
Reset all statistics now saves a full snapshot first and tells you the filename, so it can be undone from Import data.
Clearing your lifetime board now lives in one place: Settings → About → Reset all statistics.
Various fixes and visual polish.
New: Bid Wars. Leaderboards, celebrations and hype now live together in one place in Settings.

New: turn the game off. One switch strips the overlay back to your camera, ad banners, ticker and socials — no scoreboards, no confetti, no announcer. Shop offers, giveaways and Ryli's answers still speak.
New: keep dollar figures off camera. Leaderboards can show lots won instead, or just a name and a medal.
New: tidy your boards. See both leaderboards in the app, reorder them, remove a troll, or remove and block a bot so it can't bid its way back on.
New: reset what you need — today's board, the lifetime board, or every statistic. Your settings, layout, licence and backups are never touched.
Breaker Tools now has a home in the nav with a preview of what's coming.
Various fixes.
Ticker speed now applies in Flip mode as well as scrolling, and the mode picker labels are clearer.
Various fixes.
New: set your ticker rail speed — five steps from Very slow to Very fast, in Appearance & FX.
Various fixes.
Big sales keep celebrating. Celebrations used to stop at your top tier and go quiet after that. They now keep going, doubling each time — so a $200 lot celebrates all the way up.
The ticker rail takes up to three messages, and a new Flip mode holds each one still before fading to the next — much easier to read than a crawl.
Sixteen click-to-add icons for your ticker messages: shipping, packages, giveaways, your shop, your socials.
Appearance & FX is reorganised — Webcam has moved up, and you now pick your HUD layout from three pictures instead of a dropdown.
Various fixes and performance improvements.
Your overlay in OBS now picks up RYLI updates on its own, so you don't have to refresh the layer by hand.
Various fixes.
Audio fixes: Ryli's voice and your sound effects no longer go quiet after a restart, and sound works properly in the window RYLI opens for you.
Various fixes and reliability improvements.
The ticker rail is bigger and easier to read at a glance.
You can now read every release RYLI has shipped — there's a "What's new" link beside the version in Settings → About.
Your camera in the jumbotron is now FREE for everyone, on any plan. Turn it on in Settings → Appearance & FX.
Ad banner size guidance corrected: 1468 x 500 px fills the slot edge to edge. The old advice left a gap down each side.

New: Ryli Companion — an on-screen control panel you can see while you stream. Check what's running and flip things on or off without looking away from your show. Drag it anywhere, or shrink it to the orb. Only you can see it; viewers never do.
New: auto-start auctions (Pro). Ryli re-runs your listing after each sale so you're not clicking between every lot. She stops and says so out loud if a lot gets no bids.
Ryli can now tell you out loud when auto-auctions or auto-giveaways turn on or off.
Offer alerts no longer read the dollar amount out loud — the figure stays on your screen instead.
Heads up: on Windows, Ctrl+Alt hotkeys can silently never fire. Settings now warns you and suggests a function key instead.
Various fixes from a full pre-release check.
New Stream Store item: BRB Retro Screensaver — a transparent bouncing "Be Right Back" sign for stepping away without ending your show.
The Stream Store's "New" badge now tells you how many items are waiting, and the "All" view mixes overlays and Stream Deck icons together.
New Stream Store items now show a badge on your dashboard, so you know when something's been added.
An update banner appears on your dashboard when a new version is ready. Dismiss it and it waits for you in Settings → About.
Giveaway auto-restart now works — RYLI opens the next round on her own after a winner is drawn.
New: offer alerts. Ryli can tell you out loud when a viewer makes an offer on a shop listing, so you catch it mid-auction. Off by default — turn it on in Settings → Configure Ryli.
Noticeably faster on busy shows.
Verified with OBS Studio 32.2.
Insights now has one clean sales chart that shows whether you're trending up or down, in both all-time and date-filtered views.
Settings toggles have a proper on/off switch, and dropdowns highlight in RYLI blue.
Various fixes and reliability improvements.
New: Auto Chat (Pro) — have Ryli post a reminder to your live chat on a hotkey, on a timer (5–60 minutes), or both. She can say it out loud too. Settings → Configure Ryli → Talk and listen.
Various fixes to hotkeys, timers and overlay performance.

Important fix: if you left RYLI running and went live again without restarting it, tracking could stay stuck for the whole next show — no bids, chat, wins or voice. That's fixed; you can leave RYLI open between shows.
New: Ticker Rail (Pro) — an optional scrolling band along the top or bottom of your overlay.
RYLI now tells you it's still running in the tray after you close the window, with a "don't show this again" option.
Locked Pro features now show a real upgrade link instead of simply not working.
Various fixes to accuracy, stability and performance.
New: ThermalFlow (Pro) — print a label to a USB label printer the instant a lot sells.
The free trial is now 10 days.
RYLI now lives in your system tray, so closing the window hides it instead of quitting and can't drop your overlay mid-show.
Various fixes to print quality, performance and stability.
